questions.text_english:
(1) Jonathan Seagull discovered that boredom, fear and anger are the reasons a gull's life is so short and with those gone from his thought, he lived a long, fine life indeed.

(2) They laughed at him. The other gulls scorned him. 'Such nonsense', they would squawk, as he practised flying, not for food but for the joy of flight itself. But Jonathan, undeterred, flew higher and faster than any gull before him. He learned that the secret to flight was not merely flapping wings, but in knowing the purpose of flying.

(3) 'Break the chain of your thought', he told himself, 'And you break the chains of your body.'
In solitude, he mastered loops, dives and rolls. He flew at speeds that blurred the ocean below. The flock cast him out for defying tradition, he discovered that exile was not the end but a beginning. Alone, he found peace. Alone, he found the sky.

(4) One morning, soaring silently above the clouds, Jonathan was joined by two radiant gulls. Their wings shone with light and their presence was calm and sure. 'We've been watching you', they said. 'You're ready to come with us.'
'Where?' Jonathan asked blinking in the sunlight.
'To a higher level of being, they answered.
You have learned much but there is more more to flying, more to being a gull.'

(5) He followed them into a realm where flight was pure thought and time had no meaning. There, gulls didn't fight over scraps of bread or squawk at one another in fear. They flew to understand themselves to explore the limitless. There Jonathan met Chiang, the wisest gull, who told him 'The only true law is that which leads to freedom there is no other.'

(6) Jonathan began to teach others what he had learned, sharing not just flight techniques but freedom of thought. You can go as far as you wish,' he would say. 'Because you have the right to learn. You have the right to be free.'
No longer bound by rules, written in sand, Jonathan soared not just through the skies but through understanding. And as he flew, he knew that greatness is not measured in a wingspan but in the courage to break free.

sub_questions.text_english: According to Jonathan, what was the secret of living a long life?
sub_questions.solution: Jonathan discovered that eliminating boredom, fear, and anger from one's thoughts is the secret to living a long and fulfilling life.

sub_questions.text_english: How did Jonathan's unconventional passion for flying lead to his exclusion from the flock?
sub_questions.solution: Jonathan's passion was seen as 'nonsense' by the other gulls, as he flew for the joy of it rather than for food. His refusal to conform to the traditional way of life and his persistent defiance led the flock to cast him out.

sub_questions.text_english: Read and complete the following sentence suitably: 'Break the chains of your thought and you break the chains of your body', suggests: Choose the correct response: (A) freedom is achieved through physical strength. (B) mental liberation is the key to true freedom.

options.A: freedom is achieved through physical strength.
options.B: mental liberation is the key to true freedom.

sub_questions.solution: Mental liberation is the key because Jonathan realizes that physical limitations are governed by one's own restrictive thinking; changing his mindset allows him to transcend those physical limits.

sub_questions.text_english: Complete the following suitably with ONE advantage with reference to paragraph 3. It was ironical that Jonathan Seagull's exile did not mean isolation but _______.
sub_questions.solution: It was ironical that Jonathan Seagull's exile did not mean isolation but a beginning, as it provided him the solitude needed to master his skills and discover his potential.

sub_questions.text_english: What do the two radiant gulls who approached Jonathan, most likely represent? (A) rivals sent to watch his skills. (B) a hallucination formed out of his loneliness. (C) fellow gulls returning from his original flock. (D) spiritual guides leading him to a higher plane.

options.A: rivals sent to watch his skills.
options.B: a hallucination formed out of his loneliness.
options.C: fellow gulls returning from his original flock.
options.D: spiritual guides leading him to a higher plane.

sub_questions.solution: These radiant gulls represent spiritual guides who have come to elevate Jonathan to a 'higher level of being' because he has surpassed the limitations of his original flock.

sub_questions.text_english: Provide one textual evidence with reference to paragraph 4 to prove the following: You are ready to come with us.
sub_questions.solution: The evidence is the statement made by the radiant gulls: 'We've been watching you', which confirms they recognize his preparedness.

sub_questions.text_english: In Chiang's statement, the only true law is that which leads to freedom - there is no other, what does the phrase 'the only true law' refer to?
sub_questions.solution: It refers to the pursuit of truth and knowledge that empowers an individual to transcend limitations and achieve genuine, self-determined liberation.

sub_questions.text_english: Select the option that best explains Jonathan's transformation after meeting Chiang. (A) becomes more aggressive and fearless (B) forgets that past and returns to his flock. (C) learns to use his skills to dominate the other gulls. (D) internalises freedom and shares his wisdom with others.

options.B: forgets that past and returns to his flock.
options.C: learns to use his skills to dominate the other gulls.
options.D: internalises freedom and shares his wisdom with others.

sub_questions.solution: After meeting Chiang, Jonathan evolves from a self-focused learner to a teacher who understands that freedom of thought is a gift to be shared with others.

sub_questions.text_english: Complete the analogy with ONE word from paragraph 6: free : bound :: dropped : _______ (A) soared (B) learned (C) measured (D) break
sub_questions.solution: The analogy uses antonyms. Just as 'free' is the opposite of 'bound', 'soared' (going up) is the opposite of 'dropped' (going down) in context.

sub_questions.text_english: In what way did Jonathan's journey challenge traditional beliefs? Give an example.
sub_questions.solution: Jonathan's journey challenged the traditional belief that gulls flew only for food. By practicing flight for the pure 'joy of flight', he proved that there were higher purposes and greater potential in being a gull than merely following the survival-focused norms of the flock.

questions.text_english:
(1) Introduction: India faces a serious road safety challenge. According to the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, over 4.8 lakh road accidents were reported in 2023, leading to 1.72 lakh deaths. Many of these could have been avoided by simple precautions - wearing helmets, fastening seatbelts and following speed limits. These statistics aren't just numbers; they represent lives lost and family dynamics changed forever.

Causes of Road Accidents in India (2023)
S. No. Causes | %
1. Overspeeding | 56
2. Drunk driving | 8
3. No seatbelt/helmet | 15
4. Distraction (mobiles) | 6
5. Mechanical failure | 4
6. Weather/road condition | 6
7. Others | 5

(2) Methodology: Recognising this, several cities are becoming proactive, especially near school zones. The municipal corporations and traffic police have introduced stricter school-zone safety measures speed bumps, zebra crossings and digital signboards. This led to a 30% drop in minor accidents near schools, within a year. The success lay in combining infrastructure with awareness. Parents, teachers and traffic marshals helped monitor traffic during school hours.

(3) Survey: It's not just governments stepping up. In many cities, class XI and XII students launched a campaign called 'Ride Right', promoting helmet use among two-wheeler riders. They handed out stickers, ran roadshows and launched a 'No Helmet, No Selfie' challenge that went viral. Over 2000 riders pledged to wear helmets daily. Their success even led to invitations from the municipal body to speak in other schools proof of how youth-led efforts can spark policy engagement.

(4) Results Technology is also playing a significant role. Automation through AI-powered traffic cameras, digital signs and automated lights is being implemented in metros to reduce human error and improve monitoring including Pilot projects such as iRASTE and AI based road safety pilot to predict and prevent accidents using real time data and alerts for drivers. These systems have led to a 40% rise in fine collection, showing improved rule enforcement. GPS based alert systems in school buses now notify parents of speeding or unscheduled stops - another step towards safer school commutes.

(5) Implication for interventions Still, personal responsibility is the most powerful safety tool. Whether it's a student cyclist using the left lane or a pedestrian waiting for the signal, every right choice sets an example. A popular slogan in school says it best I follow, I influence. Road safety is about respecting life, valuing time, and leading by example.

sub_questions.text_english: What strategy does the author use in paragraph (1) to highlight the seriousness of road accidents? (A) use of statistics and emotional appeal. (B) humour and satire (C) technical jargon and neutrality (D) personal anecdotes and optimism

options.A: use of statistics and emotional appeal.

sub_questions.solution: The author uses government statistics to establish the scale of the crisis and pairs this with a statement about 'lives lost and family dynamics changed forever' to evoke an emotional response.

sub_questions.text_english: What evidence from the passage suggests that stricter school-zone measures were effective? (A) the number of schools increased rapidly. (B) there was a 30% drop in minor accidents near schools. (C) teachers and parents opposed the new rules. (D) students stopped commuting by bicycle.

options.A: the number of schools increased rapidly.
options.B: there was a 30% drop in minor accidents near schools.
options.C: teachers and parents opposed the new rules.

sub_questions.solution: The text clearly states that the introduction of measures like speed bumps and digital signboards led to a 30% reduction in minor accidents near schools within one year.

sub_questions.text_english: What would the following be classified as? 'Students launched a campaign called Ride Right promoting helmet use among two wheeler riders.' Select the appropriate response: (A) primary purpose (B) secondary objective (C) method of analysis (D) research outcome
sub_questions.solution: This campaign was the main proactive action taken by the students, representing their primary intent or purpose in the context of the initiative.

sub_questions.text_english: Give two points to support the success of the No Helmet No Selfie Challenge.
sub_questions.solution: The campaign achieved success by going viral, which helped spread the message effectively to a wide audience. Consequently, it resulted in over 2000 riders pledging to wear their helmets daily, demonstrating a tangible change in behavior.

sub_questions.text_english: Which word from paragraph 4 best conveys the idea of 'ensuring compliance through authoritative measures' especially in the context of traffic systems? (A) collection (B) enforcement (C) monitoring (D) automation
sub_questions.solution: The term 'enforcement' refers to the act of compelling observance of a law or rule, which is exactly what the improved traffic systems achieved.

sub_questions.text_english: Analyze why does the author emphasise that both technology and personal responsibility are important in promoting road safety.
sub_questions.solution: Technology, such as AI cameras and GPS, is crucial for reducing human error and improving monitoring, which leads to better rule adherence. However, the author emphasizes personal responsibility as the most powerful tool because safe road culture ultimately relies on individuals making the right, ethical choices to protect themselves and others.

sub_questions.text_english: Complete the following with a suitable reason: Road safety is about personal responsibility because _______.
sub_questions.solution: Road safety is about personal responsibility because every individual choice—such as using the correct lane or respecting signals—sets an example that influences others and ultimately values human life.

sub_questions.text_english: Which of the following inferences is best supported by the data in the table? (A) enforcement of helmet and seat belt rules would address the cause of road deaths. (B) speeding is the key issue, which requires technological and behavioural interventions. (C) mobile phone use while driving is the fastest growing cause of accidents. (D) drunk driving accounts for more deaths than 'no helmet/seat belt' and distractions combined.

options.A: enforcement of helmet and seat belt rules would address the cause of road deaths.
options.B: speeding is the key issue, which requires technological and behavioural interventions.
options.C: mobile phone use while driving is the fastest growing cause of accidents.
options.D: drunk driving accounts for more deaths than 'no helmet/seat belt' and distractions combined.

sub_questions.solution: Overspeeding at 56% is the dominant cause listed in the table, necessitating a mix of technological monitoring and shifts in driver behavior to effectively reduce accidents.

questions.text_english: (a) Waste management in your colony is becoming an issue of grave concern. Write a letter to the editor of a local daily, discussing the reasons for poor waste management. Also suggest ways to resolve the problem. You are Shireen/Sahil of Prestige Colony, Rahagarh. OR (b) You are Arati/Ashok from New Colony, Bamapur. You read the advertisement regarding the position of an Event Manager at Raleigh Planners and wish to apply. Write your application along with your bio-data.
questions.solution:
Prestige Colony
Rahagarh
June 6, 2026

The Editor
The Daily News
Rahagarh

Subject: Grave concern regarding poor waste management in Prestige Colony

Sir,

I am writing to express my deep concern regarding the deteriorating waste management situation in Prestige Colony. Despite being a residential area, the lack of awareness about waste segregation and an inefficient collection system has led to overflowing bins, attracting pests and creating severe environmental pollution. It is unacceptable that such conditions persist in a modern city. To resolve this, I urge the local municipal authorities to upgrade our waste collection infrastructure immediately. Furthermore, community-led initiatives are vital. We must conduct awareness drives to teach residents about the importance of segregating dry and wet waste. Civic responsibility starts at home, and the local administration must actively support these efforts by providing the necessary resources. I hope that through this letter, the concerned authorities take prompt action to restore cleanliness and health to our colony.

Yours faithfully,
Shireen

questions.text_english: (a) In today's fast-paced world, fitness apps have become a popular tool for tracking and improving health. Write an article for your school magazine educating the youth on the pros and cons of fitness apps. You are Kirti/Kirat, a school fitness coach. OR (b) Write a comprehensive report detailing the activities undertaken by students as part of the International Women's Day celebrations. You are Aarushi/Aarav, a student of class XII and a member of the school magazine editorial board.
questions.solution:
THE PROS AND CONS OF FITNESS APPS
By Kirti, School Fitness Coach

In our digital age, fitness apps have transformed into essential tools for tracking physical health. They are increasingly popular among youth because they provide personalized workout routines, track calories, and monitor heart rates in real time. However, blindly following these apps can have significant drawbacks. Many users lack professional supervision, which can lead to improper technique and injury. Additionally, these apps often raise major privacy concerns as they collect sensitive personal health data, leaving users vulnerable to data theft. While apps can motivate us to stay active, they should be used with caution, acting as a supplement rather than a substitute for professional guidance. True fitness requires a balance between technology, common sense, and listening to our bodies. By using these tools judiciously, we can work toward a healthier lifestyle without compromising our well-being or digital privacy.

questions.text_english: (a) Now we will count to twelve / and we will all keep still. / For once on the face of the Earth / let's not speak in any language, / let's stop for one second, / and not move our arms so much. (Keeping Quiet) OR (b) A thing of beauty is a joy forever / Its loveliness increases, it will never / Pass into nothingness; but will keep / A bower quiet for us, and a sleep / Full of sweet dreams, and health, and quiet breathing. (A Thing of Beauty)

sub_questions.text_english: (a) The expression 'we will all keep still' reflects : (A) the poet's willingness to keep quiet. (B) the significance of stillness. (C) the poet's appeal for collective engagement. (D) the purpose of counting up to twelve.

options.A: the poet's willingness to keep quiet.
options.C: the poet's appeal for collective engagement.
options.D: the purpose of counting up to twelve.

sub_questions.solution: The poet uses 'we will all' to appeal for collective, global engagement in a moment of shared peace and introspection.

sub_questions.text_english: (a) What does the poet want us to stop?
sub_questions.solution: The poet wants us to stop speaking in any language and to stop moving our arms, meaning he wants us to cease all aggressive and hurried activities.

sub_questions.text_english: (a) Read the Assertion and the Reason below, with reference to the given extract. Assertion: The poet advocates the importance of keeping quiet. Reason: He believes that silence can bring out profound changes in our perspective and lifestyle. Choose the correct option: (A) Both the assertion and the reason are true, but the reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion. (B) Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is the correct explanation of the assertion. (C) The assertion is true, but the reason is false. (D) The assertion is false, but the reason is true.

options.A: Both the assertion and the reason are true, but the reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion.
options.B: Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is the correct explanation of the assertion.
options.C: The assertion is true, but the reason is false.
options.D: The assertion is false, but the reason is true.

sub_questions.solution: Both are true; the assertion states his advocacy, and the reason correctly explains the underlying belief that silence triggers meaningful change.

sub_questions.text_english: (a) Complete the following statement correctly: The poet urges the people to count to twelve so that they can _______.
sub_questions.solution: The poet urges us to count to twelve so that we can have a synchronized moment to stop all activity and achieve stillness.

sub_questions.text_english: (a) 'Counting to twelve' is suggested as a _______ (synchronized/disorganized) effort for everybody to keep quiet.
sub_questions.solution: Counting is a 'synchronized' effort because it ensures that everyone pauses simultaneously, creating a collective experience of peace.

sub_questions.text_english: (a) How can the message in the excerpt, about silence and stillness be applied to promote peace in today's world?
sub_questions.solution: The message applies by encouraging people to pause their frenzied, aggressive routines, allowing for the reflection needed to resolve conflicts and foster empathy.

questions.text_english: Answer any five of the following six questions in 40-50 words each:
questions.solution:
Robert Frost highlights the selfishness of city dwellers by showing their total indifference to the roadside stand owners. While the rich travel in their luxury cars, they are too preoccupied with their own comfort to notice or care about the rural inhabitants' struggle for survival, highlighting a stark urban-rural divide. 

Sophie's father is a pragmatist who views her dreams of opening a boutique as delusional. He responds with dismissive cynicism, viewing her aspirations as unrealistic fantasies that hold no value in their working-class life, reinforcing the gap between her inner imagination and his harsh reality.

Kothamangalam Subbu was considered the 'No. 2' at Gemini Studios because of his immense versatility and loyalty. He was an efficient troubleshooter, a creative poet, and a skilled actor who could provide multiple solutions for any scene, making him indispensable to the Boss.

Rajkumar Shukla was resolute because he did not give up until he achieved his purpose. Despite Gandhi’s busy schedule, he doggedly followed him from place to place—to Cawnpore, Ahmedabad, and then to the ashram—until Gandhi finally agreed to accompany him to Champaran.

Umberto Eco displays modesty by acknowledging that his work is a result of trial and error. He does not claim intellectual superiority, but instead shares the process of his research, including his failures, showing his human side rather than presenting himself as a flawless academic genius.

Beauty is 'everlasting' because it serves as an eternal source of joy. Keats notes that as life gets filled with gloom and despondency, a beautiful object acts as a healing force. It creates a lasting impression on our dark spirits, offering inspiration and comfort forever.

questions.text_english: Answer any two of the following three questions in 40-50 words each:
questions.solution:
Tishani Doshi feels she is walking into a 'giant ping-pong ball' because Antarctica is completely devoid of human markers like trees, billboards, or buildings. The landscape is a stark, vast expanse of white, making one feel tiny and disconnected from the familiar world.

Charley realizes Sam can't return to his old business because Sam has completely embraced his desire to escape reality. By settling in Galesburg, 1894, Sam has effectively abandoned his practice, choosing the fantasy of a simpler past over the modern world he once professionally analyzed.

Derry enters Mr. Lamb’s garden seeking solitude, believing it to be empty. His intent is not to disturb anyone, but to escape from society’s judgment regarding his burnt face. He enters the garden simply because he feels it is a place where he can hide from others' pity.

questions.text_english: Answer any one of the following two questions in 120-150 words: (a) How do the characters of Rajkumar Shukla from 'Indigo' and William Douglas from 'Deep Water' compare and contrast in terms of their courage, constraints, and determination? OR (b) Analyse the lesson 'Lost Spring' and the poem 'A Roadside Stand' with reference to social inequality and the indifferent attitude of society.
questions.solution:
Rajkumar Shukla and William Douglas are both powerful examples of determination, though their journeys differ significantly. Shukla’s courage was rooted in his unyielding commitment to justice for sharecroppers. Despite his lack of education and resources, his determination to bring Gandhi to Champaran forced the hands of colonial authorities, proving that individual persistence can overcome massive political barriers. 

William Douglas, conversely, faced an internal, psychological constraint—an intense, paralyzing fear of water. His journey was one of self-conquest. Through disciplined, grueling training, he pushed past his terror to reclaim his life and freedom. While Shukla fought for a community's rights against an external oppressor, Douglas fought his own internal demons. Both men illustrate that whether the struggle is communal or personal, relentless will and courage can surmount any obstacle, shifting one’s destiny through sheer, unwavering resolve.

questions.text_english: Answer any one of the following two questions in 120-150 words: (a) In what way did Mr. Lamb's ideas of watching, listening, and thinking help Derry change his perspective towards life? OR (b) According to Tishani Doshi in 'Journey to the end of the Earth', man's supremacy over nature is responsible for the problems we face today. Support your answer with evidence from the text.
questions.solution:
Mr. Lamb's philosophy of watching, listening, and thinking plays a pivotal role in transforming Derry’s life. Derry enters the garden filled with self-pity and bitterness due to his facial disfigurement. Mr. Lamb, despite his own disability, remains vibrant and optimistic, teaching Derry that life is about more than just a physical appearance. By encouraging Derry to watch the world around him, listen to the sounds of nature, and think deeply about his perceptions, Lamb challenges Derry’s defensive mindset.

He shows Derry that beauty is subjective and that his disability need not define his identity. Derry learns that he can choose how he interacts with the world. Through Lamb’s gentle guidance and philosophical wisdom, Derry realizes that he is not a prisoner of his circumstances. He begins to see the potential for joy and connection, eventually finding the courage to return to the garden, signaling a fundamental shift from self-loathing to self-acceptance and a newfound appreciation for the richness of existence.
